cross_figure_narrative: Enlarged cells resist imposed replacement through distinct initiation, spatial and temporal response signatures (Figure 2). Distance between competing regions matters only at short range; enlarged cells resist replacement and resolve coexistence slowly mainly because of size itself (Figure 3). Spring's middle size is the supported exception in which extra accessible separation adds a substantial resolution-time contribution. Enlarged cells hold heading longer under fluctuating input — at or above the geometric expectation at weak input — and the advantage declines as input strengthens. (Figure 4). Geometry and multiple-front fractions are descriptive: erosion below the single-front geometric expectation can also occur while a single front persists. Observed migration summaries, conditional OU velocity-memory estimates and simulated polarity-heading readouts remain separate evidence.
